notes.title: v1.2.0 - The Achievements Update
notes.content:
I'm feeling a bit under the weather (cough, cough), so I'll keep this brief:

- Achievements
- Juke Box
- Improved movement
- Some redesigned levels
- Skin descriptions
- Reworked endgame
- Many tweaks and bug fixes

Regarding achievements
Only achievements related to accumulated deaths before the update will activate automatically. If you don't want that to happen, reset your saved game before starting a new game to unlock them gradually one by one (beware, you'll lose all progress!).

About the Juke Box
I'm confident you'll get the hang of it after a few clicks.

And the improved movement?
Between frustration and fun, I'll always choose fun. I've made very subtle adjustments to the movement to benefit the player—nothing that significantly affects how we move, but it further combats the potential perception of failing due to control at any given moment. The changes should only be visibly appreciated by more seasoned players.

Concerning the redesigned levels
Some levels have been touched up or completely redesigned to enhance gameplay. I doubt you'll miss any; it only affected the most lackluster ones, which have now ended up in the limbo of discarded levels. (Will there ever be a periodic rotation of levels? Only if this gains traction beyond family and friends.)

Skin descriptions?
The descriptions should make it clear to the player (or at least give them a hint) about which skins imply higher or lower difficulty in the game.

Have fun, I hope you enjoy!

notes.title: v1.1.4 - Minor Update
notes.content:
Added the option for instant retry by quickly pressing the jump button three times after death*.
 Minor graphical tweaks.


* Some people have complained about the agonizingly long wait to retry after death. Fair enough, I get it. It seems some folks are just in a hurry to embrace digital doom repeatedly, showing no interest in a profound existential reflection. So, starting today, you can hit the jump button three times in rapid succession right after biting the virtual dust for an instant reincarnation. Happy retrying!

notes.title: v1.1.0 - Rhythm Wardrobe
notes.content:
Two important changes, some improvements, and a couple of bug fixes.
Let's dive into the changelog:


 Distinct skins (see below).
 New music engine (see below).
 EnhancedSnow™
 Polished Christmas decorations.
 Resolved issue that occasionally prevented accurate death count recording. You've likely retried quite a few more times!
 Fixed a very rare & nasty bug that could cause crashes toward the end of the game.


Now let's talk about the two main changes in this update...

Distinct Skins
Now each skin will behave differently: some jump higher, others move faster. In some cases, the changes are subtle, and all of them are suitable for completing the game. Find the one that best suits your style!

New music engine
I've heard the suggestion from many of you regarding the music; you wanted to be able to hear it better with fewer interruptions. It was challenging because the music is fragmented into about 20 pieces, but after some headaches, I believe I've found the solution. The music will still evolve as we progress, but now it will do so seamlessly, attempting to adapt gradually and organically to our advancement (and it can also lead to different patterns in various gameplays, aligning with the game's philosophy). It's not a perfect solution; there might be some bugs and occasional small interruptions, but overall, it seems functional, and I'll strive to refine it over time. I hope you like it!

notes.title: v1.0.5 - Christmas is coming to Super Retro Retry!
notes.content:
In this first content update, Christmas has arrived at Super Retro Retry! Enjoy retrying it, again and again, now in a festive Christmas setting. Don't feel particularly in the Christmas spirit? Don't worry, I've got you covered! Just head through the upper door to return to the classic setting.

Furthermore, this update includes some improvements and a good handful of fixes for minor bugs. Here's the changelog:

 New Christmas setting. During the month of December, and until the beginning of the new year, the game offers the possibility of being played with a convenient festive atmosphere.
 Fixed a sound bug related to disappearing platforms.
 Fixed a very rare bug where the player could involuntarily jump when returning from the pause menu or starting a new level.
 Revised movement routines for even more precise control.
 Various code optimizations.
 Any other minor bugfixes that I don't remember.
